newsitem.title: USA: Kiwi International Air Lines says sells assets.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi International Air Lines says sells assets.

text.p: Kiwi International Air Lines Inc. said Friday the sale of its assets to Kiwi International Holdings Inc. for about $16.5 millon was approved in U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Newark, N.J.
The acquisition of the assets include the Kiwi name, goodwill, employees, equipment, tickets and certain contractual obligations.

The new company will be a separate entity that will not be subject to the bankruptcy proceedings of Kiwi International Air Lines Inc. Kiwi filed for protection under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code on Sept. 30, 1996.

Kiwi serves Newark, Chicago, Las Vegas, Atlanta, Orlando and West Palm Beach, Fla., and San Juan, Puerto Rico, with about 212 flights a week. It has been in operation for about five years and has about 650 employees.
Kiwi International Holdings Inc. was formed by Charles Edwards, who through Edwards-Wasatch Enterprises, provided the debtor-in-possession financing for Kiwi.
Wasatch also has rights in any intial public stock offering or secondary offering.
Edwards is chairman of Kiwi International Holdings, and owns more than 75 percent of the company.
